newsitem.title: CHINA: HK press welcomes Jiang Enzhu as Xinhua chief.
newsitem.headline: HK press welcomes Jiang Enzhu as Xinhua chief.

text.p: Hong Kong newspapers welcomed the appointment of diplomat Jiang Enzhu to head the local branch of China's official Xinhua News Agency, which acted as a de facto embassy under British rule.
Editorial comments pronounced Jiang an able diplomat and the harbinger of fairer political winds after years of Sino-British wrangling over Hong Kong.

"Hong Kong people hope Jiang Enzhu and Ma Yuzhen (local head of China's Foreign Ministry)...can change the unyielding image of Beijing officials and adopt a more open attitude," the Chinese-language Apple Daily said.

Britain handed the territory to China at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of colonial rule. China promised the Special Administrative Region (SAR) considerable autonomy under a "one country two systems" formula.
The Oriental Daily said that the departure of the previous Xinhua chief, Zhou Nan, meant one fewer British enemy at the agency.
Zhou was dispatched to head Xinhua in Hong Kong shortly after China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) cracked down on unarmed students in Tiananmen Square in 1989.
"Jiang Enzhu's image is very different from Zhou Nan's," the Oriental Daily editorial said.
The Ming Pao said it hoped Xinhua would stick to news gathering and not become another centre of Chinese power.
"Jiang's most urgent task is...to establish a new Xinhua News Agency which can continue to contribute to Hong Kong's prosperity through an appropriate scale and status," the Oriental Daily said.
